source_text: Et ut res absoluta paucis illuminetur exemplis, ut tam liberum sit homini sacrilegium facere velle quam nolle, tam liberum sit parricidium velle perpetrare quam nolle, tam liberum sit adulterium committere velle quam nolle, tam possibile sit verum testimonium perhibere quam falsum, tam liberum Deo oboedire imperanti quam diabolo persuadenti.
pass_a_gloss: And that an absolute thing may be illuminated by few examples: that it be as free for a human to will to do sacrilege as not to will, as free to will to perpetrate parricide as not to will, as free to will to commit adultery as not to will, as possible to offer true testimony as false, as free to obey God commanding as the devil persuading.
pass_b_english: To illuminate this clear matter with a few examples: a person is as free to choose sacrilege as to refuse it; as free to choose the murder of a parent as to refuse it; as free to choose adultery as to refuse it; as able to give truthful testimony as false; as free to obey God’s command as the devil’s persuasion.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
